etymology: Also quoting out of context: the words are real, the sentence they were in is gone.
committed_when: A quote would settle the argument and the full text would not.
tell: The quotation marks are doing the work, and the surrounding sentence has been removed.
counter: Open the source and read the paragraph. Attribution is checkable, which makes this the most falsifiable fallacy in the guide.
senses: Ascribing to someone a claim they did not make - by misquoting, by quoting a fragment, or by naming a source that never said it.
It works because the citation is true as far as it goes. Verifying a quote means opening the transcript, and most readers will only verify the part that already agrees with them.
example: *“They said the plan was dead on arrival.”* The transcript says it was dead on arrival in the Senate, which then passed it.

confused_with.tell: False attribution puts new words in someone's mouth; the straw man puts a weaker argument there.
